frequency_question: How often does a highly controversial, partisan federal election integrity or voting access bill pass the U.S. Senate within a single congressional session (approx. 2-year window)?
membership_rule: Includes major standalone omnibus bills concerning federal voting rules (e.g., proof of citizenship, mail-in ballot restrictions, or sweeping federalization of elections) introduced since 1994. Excludes routine bipartisan election administration updates or non-controversial technical fixes.

cases.name: Help America Vote Act (HAVA) - Bipartisan compromise
Freedom to Vote Act / For the People Act iterations

provenance_note: claimed 0 hits but 1 of 5 cases are marked hit; rate recomputed from the cases
coverage_note: 5 major legislative vehicles named; covers all primary partisan election reform pushes of the last 25 years.
known_gaps: Does not separately account for rider attachments in must-pass omnibus spending bills, though major voting eligibility rules are rarely successfully attached without broad consensus.
skeleton: Major partisan election bills per decade multiplied by Senate passage rate under legislative filibuster rules
multiplier: 5 distinct legislative pushes for major partisan election overhauls since 2000, with 1 bipartisan success and 0 purely partisan major overhauls passing the Senate due to the filibuster.
validity_reason: Remains valid as long as Senate filibuster rules and polarized legislative dynamics remain stable.
